digest.component_or_area: check_raw_git_writes.py policy enforcement (R3 seam composition rule)
propositions: The existing checker (R1/R2) approves raw git-adapter mutation primitives call-by-call at module granularity, but does not enforce the protocol that tracker mutations must compose atomically within a locked transaction.

Callers outside the reconciler write seam (git_adapter.py, _ref_lock.py, _ref_lock_push.py) can hand-roll non-atomic sequences of primitives like git_adapter.add() + git_adapter.commit() without a lock, bypassing the protocol rule.

R3 fires when a mutation primitive (add/commit/commit_tree/read_tree/rm_cached/update_ref/write_tree) is called from outside the seam, detected via receiver binding (import or dynamic-loader resolved module references), and sanctioned only by reasoned inline '# raw-git-ok: reason' markers.
Exact seam files (by repo-relative path, not just filename) are the sanctioned entry set where R3 never fires; read-only exports and non-git-adapter .add()/.commit() calls are out-of-scope.
Two durable reasoned markers are required: reconcile_helpers.py (binding-store snapshot selective staging boundary) and __main__.py (detached-index CAS purge).
